fixes.explanation: Shinar it is, friend. The people journey eastward, find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Put that name in your back pocket, because this plain is where the whole story happens. Good start, baker.

Goshen is a place you'll meet later in Genesis, where Israel settles in Egypt (Genesis 47:27). This crowd lands somewhere else. They find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Mixing up two place names is easy. I do it with the drawer where I keep my spatula.

Moab is a fair guess, but this passage puts the people somewhere else. Journeying eastward, they find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Shinar is the name to hold onto. That's where the bricks start stacking up.

Wood sounds sturdy, I'll give you that. But the text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Wood never makes the list. These folks baked their own bricks and let them do the job of stone. I respect a crew that takes the oven that seriously.

Keeping watch for another flood is a clever thought, and Genesis does tell of a flood earlier (Genesis 7:17). But this passage gives a different reason. The people say, “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Their reason is a name, and no flood watch is mentioned.

Room to grow is a creative guess, but the LORD never brings it up. He says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) His words are about whatever they devise, and the size of the plain doesn't come into it. Nobody in this passage is complaining about square footage.

A tower falling over before it's done would be a plot twist, but the LORD doesn't say that. He says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) One people, one language, and whatever they devise is within reach. It's like a group chat where everybody finally agrees on a time. Scary good, that kind of teamwork.

I see why you'd pick it, since that tower is the biggest thing in the picture. But the LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) He doesn't say He'll bring the tower down. He goes after their speech, so they can't understand each other.

Not quite, baker. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) They stopped building the city. That's the end of that construction project.

Nineveh has a nice ring to it, but this verse names another place. It says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) The verse even gives the reason for the name. Babel is the answer here, baker.

Erech does appear in Genesis 10:10, so it's a fair place to land. But this verse names a different spot. It says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) Babel is the name for the place where the language got confused.
